newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5 to $10 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5 to $10 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 a tonne higher Tuesday in line with gains overnight in London, traders said.
LIFFE cocoa futures gapped higher at the open and extended gains early Tuesday. At the midday break, May was up nine stg at 1,022 stg a tonne, while July rose 10 stg to 1,042 stg.

Monday, New York cocoa futures ended firmer in switch-dominated dealings. Spot May delivery closed up $6 at $1,418 a tonne after ranging from $1,422 to $1,396. Active July finished $10 higher at $1,461 after posting trades from $1,463 to $1,439. The outer months gained $7 to $12.
The nearby May/July switch finished at 43 Monday, from 39 at the close Friday.
Technically, traders said the July contract was likely to face strong resistance at a chart gap between $1,480 and $1,504. A gap above the market also looms for May between $1,452 and $1,473.
Some traders said gains would probably be limited as operators continued to roll over or liqudated Mays ahead its first notice day April 17. May open interest fell 4,021 lots Friday, to 9,556 lots.

On the fundamental front, Ghana Cocoa Board said Tuesday the country's cocoa purchases totalled 642 tonnes in the 24th week ending March 27 of the 1996/97 crop year. The cumulative amount was 299,121 tonnes.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 1 212 859 1640))
